title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The Decision of the AI Office is a concise statement outlining the key policy positions and regulatory measures the office will enforce to govern AI development and deployment. It sets clear expectations for compliance, risk assessment, and accountability to ensure responsible AI use within the organization.

summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts created to review and analyze the technical, ethical, and societal implications of AI systems. Their findings help inform lawmakers on how to regulate AI safely and responsibly.

summary: This draft calls for standardisation in AI practices and outlines the need for unified guidelines. It aims to promote safety, transparency, and collaboration by establishing consistent, industry‑wide standards.

summary: The document shows a graphic that explains how a Community of Practice drafts documents step by step. It illustrates how each draft is reviewed, revised, and approved in repeated cycles to improve quality and consistency.

summary: This document presents a visual timeline that outlines the drafting stages of a community of practice initiative. It highlights the key milestones, dates, and collaborative efforts that guided the policy from conception through finalization.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: The "Code of Practice: 1st Draft" outlines an initial set of guidelines and standards intended to govern responsible behavior and best practices in a specific field, likely involving AI. It serves as a foundational document that stakeholders can review, discuss, and refine before it becomes a finalized, enforceable code.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: The Code of Practice: 2nd Draft sets out guidelines and best practices for the responsible development, use, and governance of AI systems. It defines responsibilities for developers and users, establishes compliance requirements, and outlines procedures for monitoring, reporting, and continuous improvement.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document is the third draft of a Code of Practice for AI, outlining guidelines and standards that organizations and individuals should follow to ensure responsible AI development and use. It covers principles such as transparency, safety, fairness, and accountability, and provides practical steps for compliance and risk mitigation.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft proposes a collaborative framework for developing and using artificial intelligence in a responsible way. It highlights principles like transparency, safety, and ethical governance to guide stakeholders in shaping AI policy.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final sets out a clear framework for responsible AI creation and use, stressing transparency, fairness, and accountability. It calls on all parties to follow ethical guidelines and work together to make AI safer, trustworthy, and beneficial for everyone.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: This policy lists specific AI activities that are forbidden to protect ethical standards, safety, and human rights. It covers areas such as the creation of deceptive media, manipulation, discriminatory use, and other harmful applications, and clarifies the consequences for non‑compliance.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: These guidelines explain how to identify and classify an AI system, detailing the specific characteristics, capabilities, and functions that qualify a system as artificial intelligence. They provide a framework for consistent use of the term across organizations and projects, ensuring clear communication and compliance with regulatory expectations.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines strategies to enhance communication and collaboration among start-ups and innovators. It aims to streamline funding, mentorship, and knowledge sharing to accelerate growth and foster an ecosystem of creative solutions.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is a policy that encourages and supports startups in the high‑performance computing sector across Europe. It provides funding, access to HPC resources, and networking opportunities to help these companies grow and innovate.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The webinar slides cover key strategies for spotting and handling risks that arise from using AI. Participants learn how to evaluate potential problems, put protective measures in place, and stay compliant with regulations.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar video covers how to identify and evaluate potential risks in AI systems, giving viewers a clear overview of common threat areas and their impact. It also explains best practices for mitigating those risks to ensure safe and responsible AI deployment.
